title: Three-layer world
kicker: World and empire · presentation of the war
hook: **Vision:** the war presented in three layers — rift graph, sector board, lane board. Not finished / not playable yet as that full stack.

blindSpots.meaning: Locked design. You play the graph today — not the finished three-layer presentation.
Sectors and lanes — adventure. What you play today.
Inside one sector: slots, construction, your base — empire stage depth.
Five-lane combat when a fight is tested — the battle presentation layer.

alsoTrue: Map→battle handoff is the WIP bridge into fights; lane board is the Vision presentation of that fight.
Do not invent a fourth layer or a diary clock to glue them.

sections.title: Not finished / not playable yet

doTitle: What you do with this page
doSteps: Learn the three names so later UI does not feel like three different games.
Play the shipped graph without waiting on sector/lane boards.
When fights you play appear, expect them to feed back to the graph — see [map battle handoff](map-battle-handoff).
doNote: Stop when three layers ≠ three unrelated modes. Related: [world stage](world-stage).

mixUps.q: Can I open the sector board today?
mixUps.a: Not as the finished Vision board. Thin graph play is what you have.
No. Lawn is its own first core loop. Lane board is map/battle presentation.

mixUps.q: Do I need all three to win?
mixUps.a: Win/lose hang on fortress and homeworld. Layers are how the war is shown, not three win conditions.

mixUps.q: Is the generator required for three layers?
mixUps.a: Related Vision work — see [world generator](world-generator) — but layers are a presentation idea of their own.
